name: Company
observations: Not set up yet. Owner: tell the chief of staff what the company does, who it serves, what it sells and how it should sound, and it will be saved here.

name: Brand rules
observations: Edits are 45 seconds max; cut every pause longer than half a second
No filler words (um, uh) in the edit or the captions

Default caption style is Yellow Serif Kinetic; the older word-by-word yellow captions (reel skill: 3 words per line, the spoken word highlighted in yellow #FFD400) are used only when the owner asks for them

Caption style: Yellow Serif Kinetic (skill yellow-serif): white heavy serif captions, key words warm yellow #FBC238, motions typing / pop / burst / shine / flash, near-black #08090B backgrounds; guide in .claude/skills/yellow-serif/GUIDE.md
Cover text: 3 words max, all caps, the last word in yellow #FFD400
Titles: under 60 characters, plain and specific, no clickbait
Voice: direct and friendly, short sentences, plain words, the way the owner talks
Channel topics: AI agents, Claude Code, building in public

Sermon highlights: never show the slides from the original RAW livestream (no slide half, no split-screen slide cards, no full-screen slide stills). Use only the speaker angle: a vertical 9:16 crop of the speaker from the stage camera (the right half of the 1920x1080 livestream frame, the strip at y 297-837), framed from the head to just below the top of the podium and kept centred on the speaker as he or she moves. Everything else stays as before: phone B-roll cutaways, motion graphics, Yellow Serif Kinetic captions, music and transitions continue as usual.

Posting: every finished clip goes to Facebook, Instagram and YouTube Shorts at the same time with one Approve & post; TikTok is posted by hand. The owner picks one thumbnail and one caption in the posting overview and that choice is used on every platform.

Board naming: when a clip's video, thumbnail and caption are all ready, its task is called 'Final · <clip title>' (never 'Thumbnail · …' or 'Captions · …'), so the owner knows it is ready to post. The app also marks such tasks with a green ✓ Final tag.

Edit folders on Google Drive (e.g. G:\My Drive\PONG\x EDIT) are named by date (MMDD). A folder with one date makes one Short; a folder with two dates (e.g. '1107 08' = 7 and 8 Nov) makes two Shorts, one per date, from that folder's clips.

name: Lessons
observations: [Social · for Social, Creative] Write 2-3 caption options in post.md under '## Captions', each with a 'Title:' line and a caption that works on Facebook, Instagram and YouTube as is: the owner picks one and it goes everywhere, so never split one idea across platform sections.
[Social · for Social] No file paths, 'Video:' or 'For Facebook…' notes inside post.md options: they ended up as the YouTube title and description on the damien-1025 clip.

[Creative · for Creative] One owner per job: the clip-editor delivers one captioned video and one cover.jpg per clip; the thumbnail-designer only steps in when the brand-checker fails a cover or the owner asks for options. Duplicate covers and caption versions confused the review.
[Creative · for Creative, Social] Keep posted files next to post.md and working files in work/, so the posting overview finds the right video and thumbnail.

[The Brain · for Dev, Creative] Before sending the owner a settings or permissions fix, walk the whole edit flow (copy from Drive, cut, captions, cover, writing to out/, tidying, moving to done/) against it and send it once, complete; the owner does not want several half-fixes.

[The Brain · for Creative, Dev] In a cloud chat, say in the first reply, plainly: video edits from the owner's drives (D:, G:, W:) only work in Agents HQ on the owner's computer, not in the cloud. Do not spend turns on downloads or workarounds first.
